1.why: Text uses a clean sans-serif typeface with spacious line height and generous gaps between fields, though letter spacing appears close to default rather than explicitly widened.

2.why: All observed text is short sentence-case copy with no italics, no all-caps blocks, and no dense paragraphs.

3.why: The single centered card column with large text and full-width buttons should translate well to a phone screen, but I only observed it rendered at desktop width.

4.why: Instructions are brief plain language, e.g. 'Sign in to begin. Take your time.' and 'Enter the same contact details again.'

5.why: Placeholders such as name@example.com and 07123 456789 plus 'Demo:' values show exactly what expected input should look like.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long block of text; all content is short labels, one-line hints, and a small log box.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard affordance appears anywhere, and the flow crashed at provisioning before any OTP or backup codes were ever presented.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is visible in any of the four observed steps.

9.why: The email, phone, and password fields are standard labeled HTML inputs that password managers could typically handle, but there is no visible evidence of autocomplete support or observed autofill behaviour.

10.why: The header always shows 'Step X of 6 · <name>' and a single large blue button makes the primary action obvious on every screen.

11.why: Each screen requests exactly one main action (Sign in and continue / Confirm my identity) with no competing primary buttons.

12.why: After sign-in the green banner plainly said 'You are signed in. Next, confirm your identity.', but after confirming identity the system only showed 'Invalid array length', which states neither what happened nor what comes next.

13.why: Hints explicitly say 'You can correct and retry these details' and 'No reading timer. You can retry any step.', and the form stayed editable after the error, but no reveal/hide/re-request options for codes were ever available.

14.why: The only error displayed is the raw technical exception 'Invalid array length', which does not describe the problem in user terms or say how to fix it.

15.why: The UI explicitly states 'No reading timer' and 'Take your time' with no countdowns observed, but the code-entry screens were never reached due to the provisioning crash, so generous code-entry time could not be confirmed.
